message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became fascinated by mortal settlements when entering a city. They loved the paved ground, the intricate bridges, and above all the houses. The stone walls formed shelters from weather while connecting earth with family stories. They decided to learn housebuilding using a touch of arcane magic from a self-made staff. At first, the magic seemed simple to such a curious creature. Pebble Spring traced the seams between stones and listened for hidden rhythms. A bridge taught patience, because every span needed careful balance. A wall taught humility, because even small cracks could ruin a shelter. A roof taught wonder, because it held the sky without breaking. The staff hummed when the stones settled into their true places. Pebble Spring carved small charms into lintels to welcome weary travelers. Each charm carried a whisper of forest, rain, and quiet roots. The townsfolk noticed how the new homes felt warm in winter and cool in summer. Some said the houses were sturdy, while others said they were strangely alive. Pebble Spring was pleased by both observations, though the Leshy did not boast. A master builder finally offered to teach the old forms of masonry. The lesson began with chisels, plumb lines, and a patient ear for stone. By evening, Pebble Spring had raised a small porch that gleamed. The porch supported a bench, a lantern, and a door for future visitors. Friends arrived and tested the joinery, laughing as the wood flexed gently. Pebble Spring smiled, knowing the craft was only beginning. The next day, rain revealed a flaw in the mortar near the eaves. The builder corrected it and praised the careful attention to detail. Finally, Pebble Spring's cottage, built with patient hands, bright ideas, and a little arcane magic, pleased the whole village, even though its fresh paint wore uneven marks, making the walls look charmingly aged, slightly spotty and lovely.
